note: True only if the consumer process crashes on a live host: the kernel closes the socket and the server sees FIN/RST. If the host dies, freezes or is partitioned, nothing is sent; the server learns of it only through an application timeout or TCP keepalive, which on Linux is off unless SO_KEEPALIVE is set and starts after 7200 s idle by default. A network-connection lock therefore still needs a lease/timeout.
